title: WebSockets & Server-Sent Events

subtopics.title: Polling
subtopics.explanation: With polling, the browser asks the server repeatedly whether something changed. It is simple to understand, but frequent requests can waste work. Use it when updates are infrequent or simpler infrastructure matters. It is like checking a mailbox every minute.

subtopics.title: Server-sent events
subtopics.explanation: SSE keeps one HTTP connection open so the server can stream text updates to the browser. The direction is server to client. Browsers can reconnect automatically, which suits feeds and status notifications.

subtopics.title: WebSockets
subtopics.explanation: A WebSocket starts with an HTTP upgrade and then allows messages in both directions. It suits interactive products such as collaborative editing or multiplayer games. The application must define message types, reconnect rules, and authorization.

subtopics.title: Failure and reconnect
subtopics.explanation: Networks drop. A live interface needs a reconnect policy, connection status, and a way to recover missed updates. Use message IDs or a fresh snapshot when gaps matter. A radio needs a plan for returning after the signal fades.

subtopics.title: Accessible updates
subtopics.explanation: New information should not surprise or overwhelm people. Announce important status changes, let users pause noisy updates, and keep a readable history when possible. A live connection is a delivery method, not the user experience itself.

foundations.overview: SSE streams updates from server to browser; WebSockets allow two-way messages.
foundations.whyItMatters: These ideas affect how quickly, reliably, and safely a frontend works.
foundations.browserPerspective: The browser exposes EventSource for SSE and WebSocket for two-way connections. Both need cleanup when the component no longer uses the connection.
foundations.realWorldUsage: Choose transport from message direction, frequency, reconnect needs, and product infrastructure.
foundations.businessImpact: Reliable updates support collaboration and timely alerts without asking people to refresh.
foundations.engineeringImpact: Version message shapes and handle reconnects, authentication expiry, and duplicate delivery.
foundations.performanceImpact: Avoid high-frequency polling when a stream is appropriate; close unused connections.

commonMisconceptions.myth: WebSockets are always the best realtime choice
commonMisconceptions.reality: SSE or polling can be simpler when updates only travel one way or happen rarely.

commonMisconceptions.myth: An open connection means updates cannot be lost
commonMisconceptions.reality: Networks can disconnect; clients need recovery and resynchronization.
